title: Burned flint, wood and seeds at Gesher Benot Ya'aqov, Israel
summary: At Gesher Benot Ya'aqov, an Acheulian site beside an ancient lake in northern Israel, researchers found burned seeds, wood and flint clustered in particular spots. They read this as evidence that hominins controlled fire nearly 790,000 years ago, possibly at hearths. The finding was published in Science in 2004.

uncertainty.note: Years before present in the sources are written here as negative calendar years without subtracting 1950; the sources give rounded ages. HUJI/Science abstract says nearly 790,000 years ago; Science News says hearths were built by about 750,000 years ago, so the range runs between the two statements.

where.historical_name: Shore of an ancient lake in what is now northern Israel; no polity or place name applies

importance.justification: Cited as early evidence for controlled fire use in Eurasia.
